title: Oven-baked fish sticks
skill: Thawing fish safely and baking to 145°F

notes.text: For more than 4, use two sheet pans, one on each middle rack, and swap them halfway.

move.title: Thawed, crumbed, baked
move.body: Homemade fish sticks are strips of cod in a crisp crumb coat, baked instead of fried. Today you'll start with fish that thawed safely in the fridge, cut it into strips, coat it, and bake it until it reaches 145°F, the safe temperature for fish. A quick tartar sauce goes on the side.

why.title: Thaw it cold
why.body: Fish left on the counter warms up on the outside while the middle is still frozen, and germs grow on the warm part. Thawing in the fridge overnight keeps all of it cold.

why.title: Dry fish holds crumbs
why.body: Thawed fish is wet. Patting it dry with paper towels lets the flour stick, then the egg, then the crumbs.

why.title: One dry hand, one wet hand
why.body: Use one hand for the flour and crumbs and the other for the egg. Your fingers stay clean, and the coating goes on evenly.

why.title: A hot oven makes it crisp
why.body: At 425°F, the crumbs brown and crisp in the time the fish takes to cook through. A cooler oven dries the fish before the outside crisps.

why.title: Fish is done at 145°F
why.body: Fish cooks fast. At 145°F the middle turns white all the way through and flakes when you press it.

wrong.fix: Pat the fish drier next time, and press the crumbs on firmly.
Bake 2 more minutes, mitts on to check.
Bake 2 more minutes and check again.

wrong.sign: The fish is still icy in the middle
wrong.fix: It didn't thaw all the way. Put it back in the fridge, or thaw it in cold water in a sealed bag.

quiz.explain: The fridge keeps every part of it cold.
Flour won't stick to wet fish.

quiz.q: What temperature is fish safe at?

ingredients.prep: thawed in the fridge overnight if frozen

steps.text: Move a rack to the middle of the cold oven. Spread the pan's oil on the sheet pan. Heat the oven to 425°F.
Check the fish is thawed: press the thickest part. It should feel soft all through, with no ice.
steps.tip: Still icy? Seal it in a bag and set it in cold water for 30 minutes.

steps.text: Cut the pickle into small bits with the paring knife. Stir it into the mayonnaise in the small bowl with a squeeze of lemon.
Put the flour on the plate. Beat the egg in the shallow dish with the fork. Mix the panko, oil, and paprika in the bowl.
steps.tip: Line them up: flour, egg, crumbs, then the sheet pan.

steps.text: Wash your hands and throw the eggshell away.
Pat the fish dry with paper towels. Cut it into strips about as wide as two fingers. Sprinkle them with the salt.
steps.look: About 12 strips, close to the same size.

steps.text: Throw the paper towels away. Wash your hands, the knife, and the board with hot, soapy water.
Dry hand: roll a strip in flour. Wet hand: dip it in egg. Dry hand: press it into the crumbs. Lay it on the pan.
Wash your hands. Throw out the leftover flour, egg, and crumbs.
Mitts on. Slide the pan into the oven and bake.
steps.look: Golden crumbs, sizzling at the edges.

steps.text: Mitts on, pull the rack out. Slide the thermometer into the side of the thickest stick. It should read 145°F or more.
steps.tip: Not there yet? Bake 2 more minutes.

steps.text: Turn off the oven. Lift the fish sticks onto plates with the spatula. Serve with the tartar sauce and lemon.
steps.look: Crisp golden sticks, white and flaky inside.
